cds.text: Identify how texts have different language features and are typically organised into characteristic stages by purpose
Describe how spoken, written and multimodal texts use language features and characteristic stages and phases
Explain how curriculum texts are organised into stages and phases by purpose, noting that authors adapt structures and features
Identify how connectives (temporal and conditional words) and topic word associations sequence and connect ideas
Understand how sentence or paragraph starting points give prominence to the message and guide the reader
Understand that cohesion can be created through intentional repetition and word associations
Identify online text navigation features that enhance readability, such as headlines, drop-down menus, links, graphics and layout
Compare texts from different times with similar purposes and audiences, noting differences in how events are depicted
Describe how a text reflects the time and place in which it was created
Examine texts, including media texts, that represent ideas and events, and identify how they reflect their creation context
Identify characteristic features these text types use to meet their purpose
Explain characteristic features these text types use to meet their purpose
Analyse how text structures and language features work together to meet purpose and engage and influence audiences
Read different text types, integrating phonic, semantic and grammatical knowledge to read accurately and fluently
Navigate and read texts for specific purposes, monitoring meaning with skimming, scanning and confirming
Select, navigate and read texts for a range of purposes, monitoring meaning and evaluating structural features such as contents, glossary, headings and subheadings
Use comprehension strategies, including monitoring, to build meaning, expand topic knowledge and evaluate texts
Use comprehension strategies, including monitoring, to build meaning and evaluate information and ideas
Use comprehension strategies, including monitoring, to build meaning and connect and compare content from a variety of sources
Read and write words with more complex letter combinations, including a variety of vowel sounds and known prefixes and suffixes
Use phoneme-grapheme matches, syllables and common letter patterns that have different pronunciations to read and write words
Apply phonological and morphological knowledge to read and write increasingly complex words
Use letter patterns (including double letters), spelling generalisations, word families, prefixes, suffixes and word origins to spell more complex words
Build and spell new words from known words, base words, prefixes, suffixes, word origins, letter patterns and spelling generalisations
Spell new words, including technical words, using word origins (including Latin and Greek roots), base words, affixes, letter patterns and generalisations
Read and write high-frequency words, including homophones, and use context to identify correct spelling
Explore less common plurals, and understand how a suffix changes a word's meaning or grammatical form

sentences.text: {{S}} makes observations and supports them with evidence from the text to enhance {{pos}} understanding of stories and information.
{{S}} reads with confidence and uses context, grammar knowledge and skimming strategies to locate information in moderately complex texts.
{{S}} applies reading strategies to interpret complex texts and explains how these texts communicate meaning.
{{S}} monitors {{pos}} understanding and recognises when meaning breaks down.
{{S}} explains how authors make deliberate choices to shape the reader's perception.
{{S}} interprets key ideas in narratives and digital texts, and recognises how authors use language to shape meaning.
{{S}} comprehends digital texts and advertisements and identifies key ideas in narratives.
{{S}} identifies main ideas, understands simple inferences and explains how authors use evidence to support ideas.
{{S}} uses reading strategies to comprehend more complex texts.
{{S}} reads with confidence and uses skimming strategies to identify key ideas and locate details, and uses context to understand unfamiliar words.
{{S}} can interpret language features, explain how authors use evidence to support ideas and understands simple inferences when reading moderately complex texts.
{{S}} identifies main ideas and is beginning to recognise how language features help build meaning.
{{S}} is beginning to explain how language features, such as word choices and text clues, contribute to meaning.
{{S}} explains how a text can carry more than one meaning.
{{S}} reads texts with complex ideas and explains how the author built them.

rows.newText: {{S}} describes how spoken, written and digital texts use language features and stages to suit their purpose.
{{S}} explains how texts are organised into stages and phases to achieve their purpose.
{{S}} notes how authors choose language features and structure to suit their purpose and audience.
{{S}} explains how sentence and paragraph starters give prominence to the main message.
{{S}} uses sentence starters to guide the reader through an argument or explanation.
{{S}} explains how repetition and linked words create cohesion in a text.
{{S}} identifies how word associations connect ideas across paragraphs.
{{S}} describes how a text reflects the time and place of its creation.
{{S}} compares how texts from different times and places present similar ideas.
{{S}} examines how media texts represent ideas and events and identifies how they reflect a point of view.
{{S}} explains how different texts represent the same event in different ways.
{{S}} explains the characteristic features that texts use to meet their purpose.
{{S}} describes how the structure and language of a text work together to engage readers.
{{S}} analyses how text structures and language features work together to meet purpose and persuade an audience.
{{S}} evaluates how effectively a text engages its audience.
{{S}} navigates and reads texts for specific purposes using skimming and scanning.
{{S}} selects and reads texts for a range of purposes and evaluates how they are structured.
{{S}} uses comprehension strategies to build meaning and evaluate information from different sources.
{{S}} connects and compares ideas across texts to build understanding.
{{S}} uses comprehension strategies to compare ideas from more than one text.
